analysis.title: Macro stress, upside panic
key_insights: Cross-asset setup is stressed: bond vol has exploded, 5% Treasuries compete with equities, France is under pressure and macro trading is migrating into fixed income. Equity positioning is already washed out and VIX shows little panic.

GS flags light positioning into Q3 earnings. The GS Monetary Policy Factor is at -8, near the bottom of its 30-year range, and hedge fund US net positioning is in the 0th percentile. If the macro backdrop stops worsening, earnings could clear an extremely defensive market.

Non-dealers sold $63.7bn of S&P futures over six weeks, selling in five of the six weeks. The latest week added $10.5bn of selling, with asset managers at $11.7bn. More than 70% of the six-week move was long liquidation rather than new shorts.

Asset-manager gross longs have a strongly negative relationship with 10-year real yields. The recent 25bp jump in real yields coincided with another $5.5bn of asset-manager long liquidation. A roll-over in real yields is the key upside trigger for equities.

GS says Russell 2K systematic exposure is in the 7th percentile and leveraged funds hold record shorts per CFTC data through September 22. About $900mn of open interest has come out since September 29 after softer PCE and payrolls, and RTY funding spreads have richened outright and versus SPX.

BofA says the 10-year yield is above the S&P 500 trailing earnings yield, and the gap versus the dividend yield is around 4 percentage points. Both are near the widest since the early 2000s, so bonds now compete with equities for the same capital.

BofA's 5, 6, 7 framework: at 5% investors are historically agnostic between bonds and equities, above 6% higher yields have been associated with weaker equity returns, and at 7% multiples compress materially. Markets are in the first bucket.
MOVE rose from about 77 on September 10 to 113. The Market Ear had flagged bond vol as underpriced on that date.

GS says fixed-income ETF option volume (HYG, LQD, TLT, IEF) has more than doubled over three weeks, to roughly 2.2-2.4 million contracts on a 10-day average. Macro traders are expressing views in rates ETFs rather than equity indices.

DB argues the Fed put is weaker than in the 2010s because inflation is still above target. In 2022-23, Ukraine, the UK mini-budget and SVB each triggered dovish repricing, and persistent inflation then pushed central banks back toward tightening.
The euro reached extremely oversold levels last week and has stayed there with no momentum recovery.

MS (Savone) says foreigners have pulled about $8bn from Brazilian equities since mid-April ahead of the Oct 25 runoff. Derivatives positioning is about 3x heavier than in the 2022 cycle, so dealer gamma could amplify the result.
TS Lombard says the ECB may not step in quickly to support French bonds because of moral hazard, and OAT-Bund could break above 200bp before meaningful intervention.

TS Lombard says Japanese investors are repatriating capital from OATs and other foreign government bonds. Sumitomo's sale of its entire OAT portfolio is cited as a possible sign. France faces rising fiscal and political risk and large issuance needs with a less dependable marginal buyer.

tension_points.theme: equity upside squeeze vs rates stress
tension_points.bull_case: GS sees extremely light positioning (hedge fund net in the 0th percentile, Russell systematic in the 7th percentile, record leveraged shorts), so earnings could clear a defensive market if macro stops worsening.
tension_points.bear_case: Real yields, a 5% Treasury yield above the S&P earnings yield, and MOVE at 113 keep pulling capital out of equities. BofA says above 6% yields have historically coincided with weaker equity returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Real yields continuing to rise, since the recent 25bp jump coincided with more asset-manager long liquidation.

tension_points.bull_case: The obvious bull case for OATs is eventual ECB intervention.
tension_points.bear_case: TS Lombard says moral hazard and French political inaction could delay the ECB, with OAT-Bund breaking above 200bp first.
tension_points.what_invalidates: OAT-Bund breaking above 200bp before any ECB intervention.
